# ResNet18-Driven Facial Emotion Recognition

[![DOI](https://zenodo.org/badge/DOI/10.5281/zenodo.XXXXXXX.svg)](https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.XXXXXXX)
*(Note: Replace the DOI badge above with the one generated by Zenodo once you connect your GitHub repository.)*

## Overview
This repository contains the official source code for our paper: **"Resnet18-Driven Facial Emotion Recognition Approach Using Deep Learning for Improved Emotion Classification."**

We propose a robust Deep Learning (DL) framework utilizing the **ResNet18** architecture for Facial Emotion Recognition (FER). The model effectively classifies human facial expressions into seven emotion categories:
1. Anger
2. Contempt
3. Disgust
4. Fear
5. Happiness
6. Sadness
7. Surprise

By applying advanced pre-processing techniques (Image Resizing, Data Augmentation, and Bilateral Filtering), our proposed system overcomes common challenges like occlusion, illumination variance, and differences in facial appearances.

## Dataset
The model was trained and evaluated using a comprehensive facial emotion recognition dataset. 

You can access and download the dataset directly from Kaggle here:
**[Facial Emotion Recognition Dataset (Kaggle)](https://www.kaggle.com/datasets/tapakah68/facial-emotion-recognition)**

Please ensure you download the dataset and place it in the `data/` directory before running the training script.

## Installation and Requirements
To run this project locally, ensure you have Python 3.8+ installed. 

1. Clone this repository:
   ```bash
   git clone https://github.com/YOUR_USERNAME/YOUR_REPOSITORY_NAME.git
   cd YOUR_REPOSITORY_NAME
   ```

2. Install the required dependencies:
   ```bash
   pip install -r requirements.txt
   ```

## Usage

All the code (Dataset loading, Model Architecture, Training, and Evaluation) is consolidated into a single `main.py` script. By default, running the script will train the model and save all generated results (weights, metrics, and plots) into a `results/` folder.

### Full Pipeline (Train & Evaluate)
To run the full pipeline:
```bash
python main.py --dataset_path ./data --epochs 20 --batch_size 32 --output_dir ./results
```

This will automatically:
- Train the model.
- Save the `best_model.pth` inside the `results/` folder.
- Evaluate the model and save `metrics.txt`, `confusion_matrix.png`, `roc_curve.png`, and `precision_recall_curve.png` to the `results/` folder.

### Evaluate Only
If you already have a trained model weight file and only want to generate the plots and metrics:
```bash
python main.py --mode eval --weights ./results/best_model.pth --dataset_path ./data --output_dir ./results
```
